title: Lakshmi Ashtottara Shatanamavali Meaning: Names 33-36 (Harivallabha, Ashoka, Amrita, Dipta (second time))
desc: Meaning of Goddess Lakshmi's 108 names, numbers 33 to 36: Harivallabha, Ashoka, Amrita, Dipta (second time), with a short note on each.
alt: Goddess Lakshmi, 108 names 33 to 36 with meaning
caption: Names 33 to 36 of the 108 names of Lakshmi.
intro: The **108 names of Goddess Lakshmi (Ashtottara Shatanamavali)** are chanted on Fridays and at Diwali and Varalakshmi Vratham. This post explains **names 33 to 36**: **Harivallabha, Ashoka, Amrita, Dipta (second time)**.
takeaways: Each name describes one quality of Lakshmi: Harivallabha, Ashoka, Amrita, Dipta (second time).
Fridays are the traditional day for Lakshmi names.
Say each name with 'Om' before and 'Namah' after.

p: **Harivallabha** means **Beloved of Hari**. After the churning of the ocean, Lakshmi chose Hari and went to stand beside him.
**Ashoka** means **Free from sorrow**. She is free from sorrow and removes sorrow from her devotees.
**Amrita** means **The Immortal**. Imperishable. True wealth like virtue and knowledge never perishes.
**Dipta (second time)** means **The Shining One**. Her light removes darkness, ignorance and despair.
Offer flowers or kumkum at each name if you can, saying 'Om', the name, then 'Namah'. If time is short, chant a few names a day and complete the 108 over the week.

faq.q: How many names does Lakshmi Ashtottara have?
faq.a: **108** names, which is why it is called Ashtottara Shatanamavali.

faq.q: Which day is best for Lakshmi names?
faq.a: **Friday**, and festival days like Diwali and Varalakshmi Vratham.
